title: Redistribution inside the database
subtitle: The lattice functions that grow, protect and score concept clusters over millions of vectors without leaving PostgreSQL

stats.label: signals weighted into each cluster's pressure
lines of Rust in the sole acceptance authority for new clusters

lede: My distillation corpus is a lattice: question-and-answer units, each with a 1,024-dimension embedding, grouped into concept clusters with a centroid, a tier and a pressure score. The lattice has to grow where it is thin, stay stable where it is dense, admit new clusters only on evidence, and never let its seed units move. I built those behaviours as functions that run inside PostgreSQL, because the work is a set of index-backed nearest-neighbour queries and one atomic update, and moving millions of vectors to an application server would cost more than the work itself. Every cluster carries a saturation pressure between zero and one, higher meaning more need to grow.
quote: Fill once, protect seeds, keep history, and the lattice converges instead of churning.
evidence: In-database computation with PostgreSQL and pgvector: lattice functions that grow, protect and score concept clusters over millions of vectors of 1,024 dimensions without leaving the database.
Vector search and ANN indexes: lateral nearest-neighbour queries through an inverted-file index, so each centroid search uses the index instead of a cross product.
Transactional data redistribution: one function runs a whole schema as a single transaction, moves units in one update, and logs fills and drains with counts and a run id.
Deterministic acceptance scoring: ~11,000 lines of Rust as the sole acceptance authority for new clusters, every failed test returned as a reason.
Tunable data-quality models: cluster pressure from 8 weighted signals, four protection rules counted separately, and three presets from conservative to aggressive.
author: Corey James
